summary.oneLiner: CLC Industries Limited is a single-segment cotton yarn spinner operating a 32,400-spindle mill at Baramati MIDC, Maharashtra, backed by the Manjeet Group cotton business platform.
summary.business: CLC Industries manufactures cotton yarn using raw cotton as its primary raw material, describing yarn as "the core of all fabrics" and stating that as it produces only one product, segment/product-wise details are not applicable. Its manufacturing facility at Baramati MIDC, Pune, spreads over 70,000 square meters and houses 32,400 spindles capable of producing approximately 15.00 metric tons per day of high-quality yarn. During FY 2025-26 the Company achieved full-fledged commercial operations at the mill, while the trading of cotton constituted the major portion of turnover for the year.

currentContext.expansion: The annual report describes no new capex project, capacity addition or expansion scheme. The only expansion-type event disclosed is the completion of the Company's revival: during FY 2025-26 CLC Industries achieved full-fledged commercial operations at its single manufacturing facility at D-48, Baramati MIDC, Baramati, Pune (Maharashtra), a site spread over 70,000 square meters carrying 32,400 spindles with capacity to produce approximately 15.00 metric tons per day of high-quality cotton yarn. Forward intent is framed as utilisation and efficiency rather than new assets — the Company states it continues to focus on improving capacity utilisation, operational efficiency, cost optimisation and quality enhancement, alongside adoption of automation and eco-friendly production processes, a move toward value-added specialty yarns, and diversification into new export geographies. The Company has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture during FY 2025-26, so there is no inorganic capacity or geographic addition. No rupee capex quantum, no commissioning timeline for any new line, and no capital commitment figure is disclosed in the routed sections.

risks.note: Cotton is the sole primary raw material for yarn and is an agricultural produce whose supply and quality are subject to the monsoon. The AR states that fluctuations in cotton prices due to weather, crop production, procurement policies and international market movements may adversely impact production costs and operating margins, and that any increase in raw cotton prices makes things difficult for the textile industry, resulting in weak demand and thin margins.

The Company states it deals in only one segment and manufactures only one product, cotton yarn, from a single facility at Baramati MIDC. There is no product, segment or site diversification to absorb a disruption at that mill or a downcycle in cotton yarn.

risks.risk: Dependence on cotton trading for the bulk of turnover
risks.note: The Chairman states the significant increase in revenue "was primarily driven by the trading of cotton, which constituted the major portion of the Company's turnover during the year", with manufacturing contributing alongside. A revenue base weighted to a thin-margin trading activity is structurally different in quality and volatility from mill output.

risks.risk: Interest rate and working capital risk
risks.note: The AR states the spinning industry is working-capital intensive and that higher interest rates and limited liquidity may increase finance costs and impact profitability. The MD&A also records that debts increased to meet business losses and working capital requirements.

risks.risk: Intense global competition in yarn and textiles
risks.note: The AR flags stiff competition from China, Bangladesh, Taiwan and other emerging economies, and separately from Vietnam, Bangladesh, China, Pakistan and Turkey, which continues to exert pressure on pricing and export competitiveness. Relative competitiveness is stated to depend on raw cotton prices, exchange rates and the prevailing interest rate regime.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption and export demand slowdown
risks.note: The continuing US-Iran conflict and Middle East instability have raised crude, freight and logistics costs and adversely affected consumer confidence and demand in major textile and apparel importing markets, particularly Europe and North America. Global conflicts, trade disputes and shipping route disruptions may raise freight costs, affect supply chains and reduce export demand; economic slowdown and inflation may further weaken demand for cotton yarn.

Increases in electricity tariffs, fuel prices and other energy costs directly impact manufacturing expenses and profitability — material for a spinning mill, where the AR discloses electricity consumption of 3.35 units per Kg of production.

Shortage of skilled manpower, rising labour costs and evolving labour regulations are flagged as significant operational challenges; separately, changes in taxation, environmental regulations, export-import policies, labour laws and other statutory requirements may influence business operations and compliance costs. The Company reports only 21 permanent employees on its rolls.
